images.prompt: Natural close still-life photograph of one intact cream spiral seashell lying on its side on a dark plain wooden table. Its oval opening faces front right and the spiral tip points upper left. Soft elongated window reflection from the left, charcoal background, three-quarter camera, realistic shell texture. Vertical 4:5, 1024x1280. Full objects visible with breathing room. Natural photography, realistic materials and lighting; no text, logo, watermark, or illustration.

review.reason: Independent inspection confirms one complete cream/tan spiral shell with intact tip, spiral ridges, open aperture and clear table contact. Natural window illumination and wood texture are coherent; no lettering or art treatment.

images.actual_source_analysis: One cream and tan spiral seashell lies on its side on a dark wooden tabletop. Its pointed spiral extends toward the upper left and the large oval opening faces forward and right. The intact pale lip surrounds a visible concave interior, with ridged spiral whorls across the outer shell. The entire shell and tip are inside the frame with clear margins. Soft light comes from the left, forming an elongated window reflection on the table; the background is plain dark charcoal.

images.prompt:
Deep multilayer polished lacquer with subtle warm undertones, smooth flowing reflections, and restrained surface depth.
Preserve: Subject count, outer silhouette, openings, attachments, and contact points. Source camera viewpoint, framing, relative scale, and placement. Recognizable subject identity and existing background structure.
Coat existing solid surfaces with deep polished lacquer, keeping the source silhouette, aperture, ridges, and support contacts intact.
Use near-black oxblood, muted vermilion undertones, and warm reflection accents without decorative gold or painted motifs.
Preserve smooth original contour transitions and visible structural seams; do not add ornamental linework.
Show layered lacquer depth with faint hand-polished variation, avoiding visible brush strokes or heavy surface scratches.
Retain the source light direction and stretch soft highlights along curved surfaces without turning them into mirror chrome.
Keep the original framing, scale, object count, orientation, and empty spaces.
Let thin edges reveal a slight warmer undertone while keeping recesses deep and readable.
Finish as carefully polished lacquer with controlled gloss, grounded shadows, and no added ornament or display platform.
Change existing solid surfaces and their material response only; retain parts, silhouettes, openings, and placement.
Use the supplied photograph as the sole composition reference. Keep the entire source frame, original 4:5 aspect ratio, camera viewpoint, subject scale, and all margins. Produce at least 1024x1280 pixels. Output only the finished image.
Avoid: Gold leaf patterns, flowers, lettering, inlays, or decorative stands. Mirror chrome, wet melting surfaces, thick drips, or changed silhouette. Filled cavities, extra objects, logos, or watermarks.

review.reason: Independent comparison confirms the shell silhouette, spiral ridges, lip and open cavity remain intact and in place. Deep oxblood lacquer has flowing elongated highlights, subtle warm edge depth and readable dark recesses. No filling, melting, added gold motifs or extra objects.
